scout.purpose: When producers and collectors run at different speeds, buffer policy decides whether to suspend production, queue values, or discard intermediate updates.
scout.realWorldUse: Sensors, progress, scroll signals, logging, downloads, and UI state streams have different requirements for loss, latency, and memory.
scout.outcome: Measure producer and consumer pressure, choose buffer or conflate deliberately, and avoid unbounded queues and hidden event loss.

blocks.text: Without a concurrency boundary, Flow emits and collects sequentially: a slow collector suspends the producer. This backpressure is safe and bounded but may reduce throughput when production and consumption can overlap. buffer inserts a channel between upstream and downstream so they run concurrently up to capacity. Capacity and overflow strategy determine memory, suspension, and loss. An unlimited buffer can turn a temporary speed mismatch into an out-of-memory failure.

blocks.caption: State-like progress may skip intermediates; audit events require a bounded lossless contract.

blocks.title: Pressure policy
rows: Cancel slow rendering for new value

blocks.text: conflate keeps the latest value while a collector is busy and discards intermediate values. It suits state-like progress or sensor display where only current value matters, not payments, analytics events, or ordered database writes. collectLatest cancels the collector body when a new value arrives, which is different from dropping before collection. StateFlow is already conflated by equality and latest-state semantics; adding conflate to it has no effect.

blocks.title: Loss policy is domain policy
blocks.text: Never add conflate merely to make a slow pipeline appear fast.

sections.title: Conflation trades intermediate history for freshness

blocks.text: Choose policy from information value: must every element complete, may old values be dropped, can processing be cancelled, and how much latency is acceptable? Instrument queue depth, processing duration, and dropped counts at non-sensitive boundaries. Batching may be better than per-item processing. Tests should use a controlled slow collector and assert exact received values, cancellation, and capacity behaviour rather than relying on timing sleeps.

Production readiness requires evidence beyond a happy-path demonstration. State the owner and lifetime of every mutable value, the expected response to failure or cancellation, and the behaviour after recreation or a second simultaneous request. Exercise long and translated content, large font scale, alternate input, slow dependencies, and rapid repeated actions wherever they apply. Prefer deterministic unit tests for pure logic, integration tests at library and protocol boundaries, and device tests when platform lifecycle, rendering, accessibility, or system UI is part of the contract. Do not hide a missing decision behind a generic helper. A future engineer should be able to identify what may run concurrently, what survives, what is authoritative, and which evidence proves the implementation remains correct.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name ownership, lifetime, inputs, outputs, failure, and cancellation.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Choose the smallest API that preserves those semantics.

steps.label: Exercise boundaries
steps.detail: Test absence, failure, recreation, concurrency, and unusual input.

steps.label: Collect evidence
steps.detail: Use semantics, deterministic tests, traces, or protocol inspection.

steps.label: Harden
steps.detail: Fix the demonstrated risk and document the remaining trade-off.

blocks.text: A sustained producer-consumer mismatch converts latency into unbounded memory.

inspect.title: Remove event conflation
walkthrough: Conflation can discard payment events while charging is busy.
Every accepted payment intent requires a durable ordered result.
Use a bounded lossless queue and an idempotent persistence workflow.
inspect.expectedOutput: Every accepted event receives one observable durable outcome.

trap_check.mistake: Using buffer with unlimited capacity for a permanent slow consumer.
trap_check.why: Memory grows without bound while latency hides the overload.
trap_check.fix: Bound capacity and define overflow, batching, or upstream rate control.

trap_check.mistake: Adding abstraction or optimisation before defining the failure.
trap_check.why: The code becomes harder while ownership, correctness, or measured cost remains unresolved.
trap_check.fix: First write a boundary test or collect evidence that identifies the real defect.

challenge_intro.task: Implement and test separate pipelines for progress state, audit events, and cancellable previews with explicit capacity, loss, and latency rules.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: No required event is silently discarded. State-like updates favour current value. Tests prove exact slow-collector behaviour.
